summary: Creates the small multidisciplinary team and product practices needed to deliver King’s Edge, establish the first Student Experience Hub home and grow digital capability in evidence-led increments.
detailSummary:
The Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability will establish a sustained multidisciplinary team around the continued evolution of the Student Experience Hub. The core team will combine software engineering, product and experience design and agile delivery, drawing on specialist architecture, data, integration, security, accessibility, quality, service design, user research and service-management expertise from wider Digital and IT where needed.

In year one, the principal substantive product demand remains King’s Edge. The team must replatform the existing service and deliver the richer functionality committed through 4.1.4. Alongside that, it will establish the common Hub shell and the deliberately light-touch timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s access needed for the September 2027 first Hub release under 4.1.2. These should be treated as one coherent product direction, but not as two equally large delivery programmes.

The first-year core should therefore remain lean. The current planning assumption is a four-person pod: two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager, with hands-on technical leadership within the engineering capacity. Specialist integration, quality, research, service-design and assurance input should be drawn in proportionately rather than automatically converted into additional permanent first-year roles. If the confirmed product scope or technical discovery demonstrates a genuine gap, that additional capacity should be made explicit and costed then.

The deliverable focuses on who delivers and how they work. It will establish one transparent pipeline, disciplined prioritisation, continuous user involvement, proportionate discovery and prototyping, sound engineering and quality practices, embedded assurance, controlled release and a clear route into supported operation or clean closure.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary team or consistent product practices for turning emerging student-experience needs into working and sustainable digital capabilities.

Requirements are often addressed through conventional system change, local initiatives, temporary projects or standalone products. Demand can be difficult to prioritise, users may be involved too late, and promising prototypes can struggle to move through quality, assurance, release and support.

King’s now needs enough in-house capability to deliver a substantial King’s Edge roadmap while also using that work to establish the beginnings of a wider Student Experience Hub. The capacity requirement should be driven by the actual first-year scope, not by treating every future Hub ambition as a concurrent year-one delivery commitment.
caseForChange.opportunity:
A small multidisciplinary core with clear product practices can give King’s a faster and more disciplined route from need to supported change.

One transparent pipeline can connect prioritisation, design, engineering, proportionate research and assurance. In the first year, most product capacity can remain focused on King’s Edge while the same team establishes the shared Hub shell and simple access routes to timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s.

Specialist Digital and IT functions can contribute where their expertise is required without all of that capability needing to sit permanently inside the funded core team. The team can then grow only when live evidence, confirmed roadmap demand or operational load demonstrates that extra capacity is justified.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is generating an immediate pipeline of substantial product requirements and needs an in-house team to replatform and develop the service. At the same time, senior education leadership has asked that this work visibly begins the wider Student Experience Hub rather than remaining an isolated Edge destination.

That increases the importance of product and architecture coherence, but it does not necessarily require a second full delivery lane. A four-person core can remain a credible first-year planning assumption if the September Hub release stays deliberately thin and specialist integration, quality and assurance support is available when needed.

The first year should therefore test the team model as well as the product. Any expansion beyond the four-person core should be triggered by evidence about delivery pressure, integration complexity or live-service needs rather than assumed in advance.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s has an enduring multidisciplinary digital product capability with a transparent pipeline, clear decision rights and repeatable practices for research, design, engineering, quality, assurance, release and continuous improvement.

During the first year, the team delivers the substantive King’s Edge roadmap and establishes the thin first Student Experience Hub within the same coherent product direction. Capacity constraints and trade-offs remain visible, and any proposal to deepen the wider Hub is considered against its impact on agreed Edge delivery.

Over time, the team can expand or change shape as the live Hub and wider student-journey roadmap generate evidence about the engineering, integration, quality, research and service-management capacity actually required.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, explicit capacity decisions and consistent product and assurance practices make needs, priorities, progress and trade-offs clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, delivery commitments are visible and changes in team capacity can be explained by actual roadmap evidence.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while the team and its professional capability remain available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first harden-or-close cycle, increasing as the team becomes recurrent
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the multidisciplinary team has an approved route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the four-person first-year core from September through November 2026: two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager. Confirm named specialist support from wider Digital and IT for architecture, integration, quality, research and assurance where needed.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent product pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement, engineering and quality expectations, embedded assurance and release practices across the King’s Edge roadmap and thin Hub work.

steps.title: Prove the product capability through King’s Edge and the thin Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the core team can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap while also establishing the common Hub shell and light-touch service access for September. Use delivery evidence to identify any real capacity gaps before expanding the team.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make the team’s operating practices routine across the live Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, expand or reshape the team only where live-service evidence and the confirmed wider student-journey roadmap justify additional throughput or specialist capability.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: From November 2028 to June 2029, establish the multidisciplinary team, its recurrent staffing, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT services as an enduring institutional capability.
